name: first-campaign-regional
about: A carrier with no history: the pack holds the job and the benchmark only.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: A small fleet where dispatch knows your name

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.

output.audience: Class A drivers who meet the stated experience requirement and run flatbed or regional freight in the Midwest. They likely work in a larger fleet with longer stretches out. The pay per mile, home weekly and an assigned truck would make them stop.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile, shown over a loaded flatbed moving on a Midwest highway.
angles.proof: The opening states its pay per mile, and the work is flatbed on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Nothing has been measured for this carrier yet, so the pay rate is the plainest lead to test. Judge it against the benchmark cost per lead.

angles.idea: Lead with being home weekly, pictured as the driver's own street at the end of a regional run.
angles.proof: The opening offers home weekly, and the lanes are regional in the Midwest.
angles.why: Home weekly is a stated job fact that speaks to drivers who are out longer now. No history exists, so this is a test and not a known winner.

angles.idea: Lead with the assigned truck: a flatbed rig parked and waiting that is the driver's own to run.
angles.proof: The job lists an assigned truck and flatbed work.
angles.why: An assigned truck matters to drivers who share equipment now, and it is a concrete fact a picture can carry. Untested here, since there are no earlier results.

angles.idea: Say plainly who this is for: Class A, the stated experience, flatbed, Midwest lanes, seen from the driver's seat.
angles.proof: The job states the licence class, the experience requirement, the flatbed freight and the Midwest lanes.
angles.why: With no lead history, stating the requirement and the area up front should keep out drivers who cannot qualify or live outside the lanes.

angles.idea: Set the job's facts out as a plain list: pay per mile, home weekly, retirement plan, and a small fleet where dispatch knows your name.
angles.proof: The pay per mile, home weekly, the retirement plan and the carrier's own description of the fleet are all stated job facts.
angles.why: A plain list lets a driver compare this job with the one they have now. The small-fleet line is the carrier's own words and sets it apart from large fleets.
